node_definition.done_when: Tests with a temporary repository and crew home show the following: A run that commits twice, merges a primary branch carrying 40 newer commits, and commits once more lands through one landing call that names no commit, and its ledger row and its obligations row each list exactly its own commits and the merge. The same run's manifest, written with only those commits, is accepted; written with one of the 40 primary commits added, it is still landed and that commit is not recorded as the run's. A run whose manifest cites a commit on a branch it never merged is refused, naming the commit. Negative control: at the base revision the first test's landing is refused naming one of the 40 primary commits; the failing run is logged to docs/evidence/fragments/queued-work-needs-no-workaround/s26.html . The tests run on all_debug .
node_definition.goal: Land a run that merged the primary branch into its worktree with no hand-written commit list
